reason: The hypothesis synthesizes two separate bodies of literature—corrosion of Mg-Ti-Zn alloys (P3, P8, P10) and high-temperature oxidation of HEAs (P22–P26, P33–P35)—into a single, linked mechanism where thermal aging drives Ti-rich intermetallic precipitation that simultaneously modifies both the oxide scale and the corrosion mode. No single passage proposes this dual functional consequence of aging, nor does any passage connect Ti2Zn precipitation to enhanced TiO2/MgO oxide scale formation and increased micro-galvanic corrosion in a lightweight HEA. The idea of using a non-equilibrium HEBM+SPS starting state to then evolve both properties through a controlled aging treatment is a non-trivial integration that goes beyond the individual findings.
copied_elements: Ti-rich intermetallics (Ti2Zn) as cathodic sites for micro-galvanic corrosion
TiO2-rich surface film for passivation/corrosion resistance
HEBM and SPS processing for non-equilibrium microstructure
improved oxidation resistance from protective oxide scale
